subject: Post-call: model shortlist + benchmark pack (TPS / latency profiles)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hanae Saito <hanae@medicorp.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 10:12:00 +09:00
Subject: Post-call: model shortlist + benchmark pack (TPS / latency profiles)

Hi Hanae —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so your eng + data science teams have everything in one place.

Call highlights
- Primary user flow: clinical discharge summarization (avg. input 400–700 tokens; target summary 120–200 tokens).
- SLA target: p95 end-to-end latency <= 600ms for single-request summary (APAC region).
- Cost sensitivity: prefer lower GPU footprint; willingness to trade small quality delta for ~2–3x cost reduction.

Our recommended model shortlist (tradeoffs)
1) redwood-7b-quant-v2 — best cost / quality balance for your prompt set. Redwood-verified baseline: 95th percentile generation latency (256-token output) ~520ms, throughput ~85 TPS across a 4-GPU pool, and strong clinical NER preservation in our evals.
2) redwood-3b-q4_0 — lowest-cost option with aggressive quantization. Latency p95 (256 tokens) ~360ms, throughput ~140 TPS, but slightly higher hallucination rate on worst-case clinical prompts (we flagged ~2–3% drift vs. human labels).
3) redwood-13b-opt — highest-quality, heavier footprint. Latency p95 (256 tokens) ~980ms, throughput ~40 TPS; recommended only for narrow high-stakes routes.

Links & artifacts I uploaded
- Benchmark pack: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-med-eval-pack (contains perf traces, prompt sets, and runbooks)
- Redwood-verified perf profiles (PDF): https://redwood.ai/perf/profiles/RDW-4521
- Prompt set we ran: medicorp-eval-promptset_v1.json (attachment)

Short concerns we flagged
- Regression vector: prompts that include verbatim medication lists (we saw small precision drops for 3b quantized runs).
- Tokenization edge-cases around proprietary abbreviations — we included a small tokenizer audit.

Suggested next steps
1) Shared pilot: 48–72 hour sandbox using redwood-3b-q4_0 for the bulk of traffic + canary traffic to 7b quant. We’ll provide sample configs and autoscaling policy.
2) Quick QA: your clinical SME to run 50-case spot-check from the prompt set (we’ll annotate expected outputs).
3) If pilot looks good, we’ll produce a tight cost estimate for Dedicated capacity (commit options) and SLA targets.

I attached the prompt set and the perf profiles PDF. Ben and Marissa are looped for technical setup and evaluation notes.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Post-call: model shortlist + benchmark pack (TPS / latency profiles)

Thanks Rachel — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we kick off the sandbox:  

1) For the SLA target, you quoted p95 <= 600ms for 256-token outputs on the 7b quant. Is that for single-request cold start or steady-state? Our traffic has bursts at shift changes and we care about tail latency.
2) Can the 3b quant be pinned behind a rate-limiter / circuit-breaker so we can route high-risk summaries to the 7b quant without manual intervention?

Also — would it be possible to get a short CSV with the raw p50/p95/p99 latency numbers and the token-per-second samples you recorded? Our infra team prefers numeric tables.

If those look reasonable we’ll try to run the 48h sandbox on Thursday.

Best,
Hanae
Head of Data Platforms | Medicorp
hanae@medicorp.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hanae Saito <hanae@medicorp.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 16:28:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model shortlist + benchmark pack (TPS / latency profiles)

Hi Hanae — quick answers from the runtime side (copying the CSV export link below).

1) The p95 numbers Rachel quoted are steady-state (warm KV cache, typical batching of 8–12 requests on our 4-GPU pool). Cold-start spikes for a previously unloaded shard can add ~150–250ms at tail. We recommend a short warmup traffic pattern at pilot start (5–10 sustained RPS for 10–15 minutes) to avoid those spikes.

2) Yes — you can define a routing policy in Redwood Console: route by label (metadata) and percent. We usually recommend: 90% -> 3b-q4_0, 10% -> 7b-quant with automatic fallback to 13b-opt if the 7b pool is at capacity. That policy will act as a circuit-breaker during spikes.

CSV & raw numbers (short sample)
- redwood-3b-q4_0: p50=210ms, p95=360ms, p99=620ms, TPS(avg)=140
- redwood-7b-quant-v2: p50=300ms, p95=520ms, p99=950ms, TPS(avg)=85
- redwood-13b-opt: p50=760ms, p95=980ms, p99=1.5s, TPS(avg)=40

Link to full CSV export: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1perf-csv-med-4521/view  

Operational notes
- Autoscaling: set min capacity to 2 nodes for pilot traffic and enable scale-up thresholds at 70% GPU utilization.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for repeated templates (we saw up to 30% reduction in end-to-end latency for cached flows).

I can spin up the sandbox details and a sample routing policy once you confirm Thursday.

—Marissa
Sr Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Perfect — thanks for the quick answers Marissa. Hanae — we’ll proceed with the plan:  

- Thursday kickoff: 48h sandbox (redwood-3b-q4_0 as primary, 10% traffic to redwood-7b-quant-v2). Marissa will create the routing policy and upload the CSV to the Drive link above.
- Your infra team will get a read-only sandbox API key and sample config; we’ll include an ops runbook with warmup and autoscale presets.
- Deliverables during the pilot: perf CSV, annotated prompt-set with failure cases, ticket with remediation suggestions for tokenizer edge-cases.

Two quick asks from our side before Thursday:  
1) Confirm the pilot contact for your infra team (name + email).
2) Share a short list of 25 representative cases for the SME spot-check. We’ll pre-annotate expected outputs.

If that works, I’ll schedule the kickoff for 0800 JST on Thursday and send the sandbox key later today.

Thanks — excited to get this running.
Rachel
